footnotes: This instrument is probably identical with 1721 Kodisch instrument.
signature: :   "Macht 1727 / Johann Carl Kodisch in Nürnbrg [sic]"; below, initials "I C K";  horse. Bell-stay and garland decorated with flower and leaf motifs.²
mouthpiece: not orig.; looks like a trumpet mp; diam or rim 34, rim 6, throat 4.7, stem 77, exit 8.2, total length 94.7.
dimensions: L 2645 (Klaus; my meas. 2640) H 1105 (Klaus), be 125 (my meas. 124); bo 11,³  slide sec. 1669, bo1 9.8, bo2 9.9 (repair: new tube for last 70.5), overlap 28, mp entry 11.1, slide sec. exit 9.9, bell sec. entry 11.6, neckpipe at bow 14, bellpipe at bow 12;
provenance: Gift of Paul Sacher; ex coll Otto Lobeck, Apenzell.
remarks: Examined by the author, June 1999; bell has sharp terminal flare, a Kodisch trademark; tubular stays; moveable stay telescopic; slide bow has no ring or saddle, but long curved guard; ferrules at slide bow have fine decoration (dragon-scale pattern), typical of Kodisch; ferrules at slide bow are plainer, with ring pattern; bell stay similar to Vermillion specimen—flat, “toothed” design, with hole, finely decorated with floral pattern; saddle in bell-bow has ring, zigzg pattern. Rim wire has cord pattern; shell pattern at upper edge of garland; inscription on garland somewhat crude. Since the instrument is dated after Kodisch’s death, it is likely that the instrument was finished by his son, or by someone else in his workshop.
